Big Sky Industrial Inc. Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results and Highlights Phase 1 Construction Progress at Big Sky Carbon Hub

 

 

HOUSTON, November 10, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) — Big Sky Industrial Inc. (NASDAQ: BSIN) (“Big Sky Industrial” or the “Company”), an integrated industrial gas, energy, and carbon management company, today reported financial and operating results for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, while highlighting construction and development progress during the quarter at the Company’s Big Sky Carbon Hub, its flagship project in Montana.

 

MANAGEMENT COMMENTS

 

“The third quarter was about execution, and we are pleased with where the project stands,” said Ryan Smith, President and Chief Executive Officer of Big Sky Industrial. “Our in-field gathering and injection lines are complete, and our long-lead equipment has been procured, including the natural gas-fired generators that will power the plant. Plant fabrication is underway, on-site civil work begins in the coming weeks, and construction remains on schedule. We are targeting first production in spring 2027, a window that leaves sensible room for commissioning and the Montana winter. From day one, our helium is sold under a five-year, 100% take-or-pay contract. In October, the Department of Energy designated helium a critical material, which underscores the value of the domestic supply we are building in Montana.

 

“Our Big Rose MRV plan is in the final stage of the EPA’s approval process. We submitted the plan in October 2025 and, because of the federal government shutdown, it was accepted by the agency in November 2025. Historically, EPA approvals of comparable plans have generally taken 12 months or longer, so our timing is in line with precedent, even if we had hoped for a quicker outcome. Our materials are complete, nothing in the agency’s feedback has changed our expectation of approval, and while the timing of a final decision rests with the EPA, we remain confident in the outcome. On the financing side, we are in discussions on a new, larger credit facility that would expand our borrowing capacity and financial flexibility, and our 45Q monetization discussions are progressing. The path to first production is clear, and we are executing against our plan.”

 

THIRD QUARTER 2026 STRATEGIC AND OPERATIONAL HIGHLIGHTS

 

 

●

 Phase 1 Processing Facility Fabrication Underway. Fabrication of the modular Phase 1 processing facility for the Big Sky Carbon Hub has begun under the Company’s fixed-scope engineering, procurement, and construction (“EPC”) agreement with CANUSA EPC. Equipment installation at the site is planned from late in the fourth quarter of 2026 into the first quarter of 2027, and the schedule allows for winter weather in Montana. The plant is designed to produce approximately 14 MMcf of high-purity helium per year and to capture and permanently sequester or utilize approximately 125,000 metric tons of CO₂ annually at initial operations.

 

 

●

 Five-Year, 100% Take-or-Pay Helium Offtake in Place. In April 2026, the Company executed a five-year helium sales agreement with an investment-grade global industrial gas company for the sale of contained helium produced at Big Sky. The contract is structured as 100% take-or-pay over a five-year initial term at a fixed, all-in price of $285 per Mcf realized at the plant gate, with CPI-linked escalation beginning March 1, 2028, and a year-three pricing redetermination. The buyer is responsible for all transportation, logistics, and downstream delivery, so the Company realizes the full $285 per Mcf at the plant gate with no midstream or delivery deductions. The agreement provides contracted revenue from first production.

 

 

●

 Expanded Credit Facility and 45Q Financing Advancing. The Company is advancing two complementary financing processes. It is in discussions on a new, larger senior secured credit facility that would expand its borrowing capacity and financial flexibility. In parallel, discussions on monetizing its Phase 1 Section 45Q tax credits are progressing.

 

 

●

 Big Rose MRV Plan in Final Stage of EPA Approval Process. The Company has submitted two Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification (“MRV”) plans to the EPA. The Big Rose plan and its associated injection well are where the Company plans to sequester the CO₂ captured in Phase 1 as well as future phases. The plan was submitted on October 9, 2025 and, following the federal government shutdown, was accepted by the EPA on November 12, 2025. The plan is now in the final stage of the EPA’s approval process. Historically, EPA approvals of comparable plans have generally taken 12 months or longer. The Company has addressed the EPA’s comments and is awaiting final agency action. The Cut Bank plan, which was submitted on December 17, 2025, supports the Company’s CO₂-enhanced oil recovery development at its Cut Bank field over the longer term as the Company moves through future phases. That plan also continues to move through the EPA process. MRV approval is not a condition to starting the Phase 1 plant or selling helium.

 

 

●

 In-Field Gathering and Injection Lines Complete. Installation of the in-field lines connecting the Company’s production wells to the processing facility and carrying CO₂ to the Big Rose injection well has been completed. The Company’s three production wells are drilled, completed, and ready for tie-in to the installed gathering lines, and two Class II permitted injection wells are operational.

 

 

●

 Phase 2 Planning Underway. Engineering and planning are underway for Phase 2, a second processing plant on the same footprint that would use the Company’s existing infrastructure, permits, and field operations. A final investment decision on Phase 2 is expected in the coming months. The Company expects to provide additional detail as planning progresses.

 

  ● Helium Added to U.S. Critical Materials List. On October 23, 2026, the U.S. Department of Energy designated helium a critical material under the Energy Act of 2020, citing helium’s essential role in semiconductor manufacturing and other advanced technologies, as well as growing supply chain risk. The Company believes the designation underscores the strategic value of secure, domestic helium supply such as the Big Sky Carbon Hub.

 

NEXT MILESTONES

 

  ● Big Rose MRV Approval. In the final stage of the EPA approval process. Timing of a final determination rests with the EPA.

 

  ● Phase 1 Plant Installation. On-site civil work beginning in the coming weeks, with equipment installation from late in the fourth quarter of 2026 into the first quarter of 2027.

 

  ● Expanded Credit Facility. Discussions ongoing on a new, larger senior secured credit facility.

 

  ● Section 45Q Credit Monetization. Discussions ongoing and progressing.

 

  ● First Production and First Helium Sales. Spring 2027.

 

  ● Phase 2 Final Investment Decision. To follow completion of financing and final plant sizing.

Third QUARTER 2026 FINANCIAL RESULTS

 

Third quarter 2026 production was 30,628 barrels of oil equivalent (“BOE”) (76% oil), compared to 35,326 BOE in the third quarter of 2025. For the third quarter 2026 revenue totaled $2.0 million (93% oil), compared to third quarter of 2025 revenue of $1.7 million. Third quarter 2026 realized average sales prices of $77.30/bbl and $3.35/mcf for oil and natural gas, respectively, resulting in an average realized price of $63.83/BOE as compared to third quarter 2025 which averaged $60.12/bbl, $2.82/mcf for oil and natural gas, respectively, resulting in an average realized price of $49.20/BOE. Revenue increased 12% year over year, as a 30% increase in the average realized price per BOE more than offset lower volumes. The decline in production primarily reflects the Company’s 2025 divestitures of its Wyoming and West Texas properties and natural production declines in its remaining assets. As previously communicated, the legacy asset monetization program funded the Company’s pivot to its industrial gas, energy, and carbon management platform.

 

Third quarter 2026 lease operating expense totaled $2.1 million, compared to $1.0 million for the third quarter 2025. The increase reflects approximately $1.2 million of remediation and related costs associated with the previously disclosed release of produced fluids from a gathering line in the Company’s legacy oil operations, which was identified and remediated during the quarter. The Company has submitted a claim under its general liability insurance policy, which provides $1.0 million of coverage for pollution clean-up costs after a $0.1 million per-occurrence deductible, and the Company expects to recover up to $1.0 million of these costs. Due to the claim pending approval, no insurance receivable was recognized as of September 30, 2026. Excluding these costs, lease operating expense was $0.9 million, or $29.71 per BOE, compared to $29.58 per BOE in the third quarter of 2025.

 

Cash general and administrative expense totaled $1.6 million for the third quarter 2026 compared to $1.7 million for the third quarter 2025. The decrease primarily reflects lower accounting and tax professional fees. On a sequential basis, cash general and administrative expense declined from $1.8 million in the second quarter of 2026. Equity compensation expense totaled $0.6 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $0.4 million for the third quarter of 2025.

 

Big Sky Industrial reported a net loss of $3.5 million, or ($0.07) per share during the third quarter 2026, compared to a net loss of $3.3 million, or ($0.10) per share in the third quarter of 2025, which included a $0.9 million impairment of oil and natural gas properties. Adjusted EBITDA, which excludes $1.2 million of environmental remediation costs, was $(0.8) million, compared to $(1.3) million in the third quarter of 2025.

ABOUT BIG SKY INDUSTRIAL INC.

 

Big Sky Industrial Inc. (NASDAQ: BSIN) is a Houston-based industrial gas, carbon management, and energy company with operations focused on the Big Sky Carbon Hub and Cut Bank oil field in Montana’s Kevin Dome region. The Company’s asset base supports three distinct business lines: helium production, carbon management, and low-decline oil production. Big Sky Industrial is focused on developing an integrated platform that leverages helium, which the U.S. Department of Energy has designated a critical material, carbon management opportunities supported by Section 45Q federal tax credits, and conventional oil production from its owned and operated assets. The Company’s operations are designed to generate revenue from multiple independent sources across helium, carbon management, and oil. For more information, please visit www.bigskyindustrialinc.com.

ADJUSTED EBITDA RECONCILIATION

 

In addition to our results calculated under generally accepted accounting principles in the United States (“GAAP”), in this earnings release we also present Adjusted EBITDA. Adjusted EBITDA is a “non-GAAP financial measure” presented as supplemental measures of the Company’s performance. It is not presented in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States, or GAAP. The Company defines Adjusted EBITDA as net income (loss), plus net interest expense, net unrealized loss (gain) on change in fair value of derivatives, income tax (benefit) expense, deferred income taxes, depreciation, depletion, accretion and amortization, one-time costs associated with completed transactions and the associated assumed derivative contracts, non-cash share-based compensation, transaction related expenses, transaction related acquired realized derivative loss (gain), loss (gain) on marketable securities, and environmental remediation costs, net of related insurance recoveries. Company management believes this presentation is relevant and useful because it helps investors understand Big Sky Industrial’s operating performance and makes it easier to compare its results with those of other companies that have different financing, capital and tax structures. Adjusted EBITDA is presented because we believe it provides additional useful information to investors due to the various noncash items during the period. Adjusted EBITDA has limitations as an analytical tool, and you should not consider it in isolation, or as a substitute for analysis of our operating results as reported under GAAP. Some of these limitations are: Adjusted EBITDA does not reflect cash expenditures, or future requirements for capital expenditures, or contractual commitments; Adjusted EBITDA does not reflect changes in, or cash requirements for, working capital needs; Adjusted EBITDA does not reflect the significant interest expense, or the cash requirements necessary to service interest or principal payments, on debt or cash income tax payments; although depreciation and amortization are noncash charges, the assets being depreciated and amortized will often have to be replaced in the future, and Adjusted EBITDA does not reflect any cash requirements for such replacements; and other companies in this industry may calculate Adjusted EBITDA differently than the Company does, limiting its usefulness as a comparative measure.

 

The Company’s presentation of this measure should not be construed as an inference that future results will be unaffected by unusual or nonrecurring items. We compensate for these limitations by providing a reconciliation of this non-GAAP measure to the most comparable GAAP measure, below. We encourage investors and others to review our business, results of operations, and financial information in their entirety, not to rely on any single financial measure, and to view this non-GAAP measure in conjunction with the most directly comparable GAAP financial measure.
